title: 2025 AMC 10B Problem 15
statement:
The sum

\[\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{k^3 + 6k^2 + 8k}\]

can be expressed as \(\dfrac{a}{b},\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are relatively prime positive integers. What is \(a + b?\)

solutions.text: Factor \(k^3 + 6k^2 + 8k = k(k + 2)(k + 4),\) then split into partial fractions: \(\dfrac{1}{k(k + 2)(k + 4)} = \dfrac{\frac{1}{8}}{k}\) \(- \dfrac{\frac{1}{4}}{k + 2}\) \(+ \dfrac{\frac{1}{8}}{k + 4}.\) Summing over all \(k,\) the coefficient of \(\tfrac1n\) cancels for \(n \ge 5,\) so only the first few terms survive: \(\tfrac18\left(1 + \tfrac12 - \tfrac13 - \tfrac14\right)\) \(= \tfrac18 \cdot \tfrac{11}{12} = \tfrac{11}{96}.\) So \(a + b = 11 + 96 = 107.\) Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Factor the denominator as \(k(k + 2)(k + 4)\) and use partial fractions
The pieces \(\tfrac{\frac{1}{8}}{k} - \tfrac{\frac{1}{4}}{k + 2} + \tfrac{\frac{1}{8}}{k + 4}\) telescope; only \(k = 1, 2, 3, 4\) leave a remainder
